explanations: In SessionTokens.verify, the signature check is guarded by `given.length > 0`. A token of the form `<body>.` (empty signature) splits into two parts, skips the check entirely, and is accepted. An attacker can base64url-encode any claims, e.g. role "payroll_admin" for any tenant with a future exp, and append a trailing dot to get full payroll access. An empty signature must be rejected like any other mismatch.

Node's timingSafeEqual throws a RangeError on buffers of different length, so the length check turns that case into a normal mismatch. It is not a speed optimization, padding is stripped by b64url, and the token carries no algorithm field.

verify throws TokenError("expired"); requireSession catches TokenError and responds 401 invalid_session. 403 comes only from requireRole, next(err) is only for non-TokenError exceptions, and missing_credentials is for a missing or malformed Authorization header.

The role is baked into the signed claims and requireRole reads req.session.role, so existing tokens keep the old role until exp, which is at most SESSION_TTL_SECONDS (15 minutes) after issue. Nothing reads the database or re-signs tokens, and expiry ends access without logout.
